The petitioners claim to be the owners in possession of the land measuring 04 marlas falling in khasra No. 217/95 situate in Village Chak Sona Nupa, Kathua ["subject land"] which was sought to be acquired by the Collector, Land Acquisition, Kathua on the request of Kathua Municipal Council in the year, 1996.

The Collector, Land Acquisition issued a notification No. LA/45-53 dated 09.05.1996 under Section 4(1) of the J&K Land Acquisition Act, Svt. 1990 ["the Act"] which was followed by notification by the Government issued under Sections 6 & 7 of the Act on 18.11.1996,
whereby a declaration was made that the subject land was needed for public purpose and the Collector, Land Acquisition (Deputy Commissioner, Kathua) was directed to take order for acquisition.

It seems that in view of the serious objection taken by the petitioners to the acquisition,
the matter remained pending with the Collector for disposal of objections for pretty long time.

When the Collector, Land Acquisition failed to pass the award within stipulated period as provided under Section 11-B of the Act, the petitioners approached this Court by way of the instant petition seeking Parmeshwari Devi And Anr vs State And Ors on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155420855/

sentences.text: inter -
alia writ of Certiorari to quash the process of acquisition undertaken by the Collector, Land Acquisition, Kathua.

2. On being put on notice, the Collector, Land Acquisition, Kathua has filed its statement of facts in which the manner in which the acquisition proceedings were initiated has been delineated in detail.

The Collector, Land Acquisition is on record to say that the declaration under Section 6 of the Act was issued on 18.11.1996 and, therefore, it was obliged to pass the final award within a period of 02 years as provided under Section 11-B of the Act.

3. Before we proceed further, we deem it appropriate to set out the provisions of Section 11-B of the Act hereinbelow:-
"11-B. Period within which an award shall be made.-- The Collector shall make an award under section 11within a period of two years from the date of the publication of the declaration and if no award is made within that period, the entire proceedings for the acquisition of land shall lapse :
Provided that in case where the said declaration has been published before the commencement of the State Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1997, the award shall be made within a period of two years from such commencement"

From the reading of Section 11-B, it would transpire that the Collector, Land Acquisition is under the statutory obligation to make final award in terms of Section 11 within a period of two years from the date of the publication of the declaration and if no award is made within that period, the entire proceedings for the acquisition of land shall lapse.
4. Proviso appended to Section 11-B, however, provides that in case the declaration under Section 6 of the Act has been published before the commencement of the State Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1997, then the award shall be made within a period of two years from such commencement.

In the instant case, the declaration under Section 6 of the Act was published on 18.11.1996 i.e. prior to the commencement of the State Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1997 which came into force w.e.f 10.04.1997.
5.
That being the position, the Collector, Land Acquisition, Kathua was under an obligation to pass the award in the instant case by or before 09.04.1999.
It is a fact that no such award was passed during the aforesaid period.
As a matter of fact, the Collector, Land Acquisition, as is disclosed by him in his affidavit, has not passed any award even as on date.
That being the position, the entire proceedings for acquisition have lapsed.

6. We would like to point out that the only exception in the matter is where the acquisition proceedings or any action to be taken in pursuance of the declaration under Section 6 is stayed by an order of the Court.
In such situation, while computing the period of two years, the period during which the proceedings have remained stayed by a competent Court of jurisdiction is required to be excluded.

There is another exception where the proceedings would not lapse despite the fact that the Parmeshwari Devi And Anr vs State And Ors on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155420855/

sentences.text: Collector, Land Acquisition has failed to pass the award within the period stipulated under Section 11 of the Act and this exception is where the urgency provisions under Section 17 of the Act have been invoked and the twin conditions i.e. 80 percent of the tentatively assessed compensation has been paid to the land losers and the possession of the land taken over.
In such situation, the land would vest in the State.

The lapse of proceedings under Section 11-B of the Act, as is authoritatively held by the Supreme Court, cannot reverse the clock and revert the land to the land losers after it has legally vested in the State.

7. Be that as it may, for the reasons stated above and also in view of the fair stand taken by the Collector, Land Acquisition, the entire proceedings for acquisition taken by the Collector, Land Acquisition, Kathua have lapsed.

We have taken note of the reply filed by the Municipal Council,
Kathua, where it has shown its desire to acquire the land for construction of a pathway.
8. For the foregoing reasons, this petition is allowed.

The acquisition proceedings initiated by the Collector, Land Acquisition, Kathua in terms of its notification issued under Section 4(1) of the Act dated 09.05.1996 are declared having lapsed in terms of Section 11-B of the Act.
The petitioners are in possession of the subject land and therefore, shall be free to use and utilize the same in the manner they like in accordance with law.

9. We make it clear that notwithstanding the lapse of proceedings and the judgment passed by us,
the Municipal Council, if so desires, shall be free to place fresh indent for the acquisition of the subject land.
In such eventuality, the Collector, Land Acquisition concerned shall proceed to acquire the land in accordance with law of acquisition in vogue as on date.

10. Disposed of.
 (RAJESH SEKHRI) (SANJEEV KUMAR)
 JUDGE JUDGE JAMMU 20.04.2023
